overview: New this season: a Week 18 All-Star Game closes out the year. Every manager sends one player from their own roster into a league-wide All-Star pool, and the two teams with the worst records — the ones holding the 1st and 2nd overall picks in the following rookie draft — draft full All-Star rosters from that pool and face off head-to-head. Win, and every manager whose player is on the winning roster banks extra FAAB for next season.
steps: Every manager selects one player from their own active roster to nominate for the All-Star pool. With 12 teams, that's 12 nominated players.

The two teams with the worst records for the season — the teams picking 1st and 2nd overall in the following rookie draft — become the two All-Star captains: "Team A" (worst record, picks 1st) and "Team B" (2nd-worst record).
Each captain automatically keeps their own nominated player. That leaves 10 nominated players — one from each of the other 10 teams — in the draftable pool.

Team A and Team B run a linear draft (straight turn order, not snake) for those 10 pooled players: Team A picks, then Team B, then Team A, then Team B, and so on until the pool is empty. Team A goes first since they finished with the worse record.
Once the draft wraps up, each captain has a 6-player All-Star roster: their own nominee plus 5 players drafted from the pool.
Team A's 6 players face Team B's 6 players in a Week 18 exhibition matchup, scored the same way as any other week.

Whichever side scores more wins. Every manager whose player ended up on the winning roster — not just the captain — starts next season with an extra 15 FAAB, even if their own team finished nowhere near the bottom 2.
